sections.html:
Homewood is a city in southeastern Jefferson County and part of the Birmingham metropolitan area. It sits on the side of Red Mountain, due south of downtown Birmingham, at about 705 feet above sea level.

The city covers 8.31 square miles, so it is compact and almost entirely developed. ZIP codes are 35209, 35219 and 35259, and the area codes are 205 and 659. Shades Creek, part of the Cahaba River system, runs through the city.

With so little land, there is no outlying rural area, and a seller is competing mainly with houses in the same few neighborhoods.

sections.h2: How did Homewood become a city?
sections.html:
Homewood was incorporated on December 29, 1926. Hollywood, a separate town that developer Clyde Nelson began as a subdivision in 1926, was annexed on October 14, 1929, and Oak Grove followed in 1955.

Nelson sold Hollywood to Birmingham residents with the slogan "Out of the Smoke Zone, Into the Ozone." Architect George P. Turner designed many of its houses in Spanish Colonial Revival style, with some English Tudor touches. The Hollywood Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2002 and covers 815 acres with 412 contributing buildings.

If your house is inside that district, its age and style are selling points for some buyers and a restriction for others who plan large changes, so mention it early.

sections.h2: What do the Homewood numbers look like?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 26,414 residents in Homewood, and the Census Bureau estimates 28,118 for 2025, a gain of 6.5 percent. The median age is 31.3, and 34.3 percent of households have children under 18.

The rental vacancy rate is notably higher than the homeowner rate, so a landlord with an empty rental is carrying tax and insurance costs while waiting for a tenant.

sections.h2: How dense is Homewood, and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Homewood had about 3,192 people per square mile in 2020, and every resident lived in an urban area. Of the 9,770 households, 46.6 percent were married-couple households and 31.6 percent were people living alone.

High density usually means smaller lots and houses close to their neighbors. Buyers pay attention to fences, drainage, parking and shared property lines, so a survey or a plat from the county records can help answer questions before they come up.

  • Gather a copy of the plat for your subdivision from the probate office
  • Note any drainage issues near Shades Creek or on a slope
  • Be ready to say which lot lines and fences belong to you

Homewood has its own public school system. The Homewood City School District includes five schools.

  • Shades Cahaba Elementary School
  • Edgewood Elementary School
  • Hall-Kent Elementary School
  • Homewood Middle School
  • Homewood High School

Samford University is also located in Homewood. Families often shop for houses based on school attendance, so a seller who can name the elementary school for the address gives buyers an easy starting point.

sections.h2: What is under Homewood, and why does it matter?
sections.html:
Jefferson County lies atop iron, coal and limestone deposits, and Homewood sits on the slope of Red Mountain, with a city elevation of about 705 feet. On a sloped lot, grading and drainage deserve a close look before you list.

A buyer's inspector will look at foundations, grading and basements on sloped lots, so note any past repairs and keep receipts. Hollywood, the district annexed in 1929, grew after developer Clyde Nelson ran the area's first autobus line and extended a natural gas pipeline into Shades Valley to support his subdivision.

sections.h2: How is Homewood governed, and what changed recently?
sections.html:
Voters approved a move from a mayor-council government to a council-manager government in September 2024, and the change took effect in November 2025. A mayor elected by all voters leads a council that includes four members, one from each of four wards.

For homeowners the practical point is to check with city hall for current permit and code rules, because administration may be organized differently than in older guidance you find online.

sections.h2: How do people get around Homewood?
sections.html:
Max Transit bus service, run by the Birmingham-Jefferson County Transit Authority, serves Homewood. The city sits directly south of Birmingham, over Red Mountain, so downtown is the nearest major destination.

Transit access and closeness to the city are features worth noting when you describe a house to a buyer.

sections.h2: Where are deeds recorded for a Homewood sale?
sections.html:
Deeds for Jefferson County are recorded at the Probate Court, which has a Birmingham Division at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and a Bessemer Division at 1801 3rd Avenue North. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

The recording office says it cannot run a title search or prepare or revise a deed. It suggests that people use a title company or an attorney, and it notes that records are public and many can be viewed on its website.

Copies made in the Record Room cost $1.00 per page, plats are $15.00 per page, and certification adds $2.00 per document.

  • State deed tax: 50 cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1
  • A form stating the actual price accompanies the deed
  • The probate office calculates the tax when the deed is filed

sections.h2: When are property taxes due in Homewood?
sections.html:
The Alabama Department of Revenue says the lien date is October 1 and the taxes are due the following October 1, and that they are delinquent after December 31. Assessment happens locally at the county courthouse.

At closing, the title company usually splits the year's tax between seller and buyer by the day, so confirm the current bill before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What options does a Homewood seller have?
sections.html:
Homewood sellers can list, sell privately, or accept a cash offer. A well-kept house suits a listing, while a house with problems is harder to place on the open market.

  • Choose a listing if the house is ready to show and you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Choose a private sale if you want to skip a commission and can handle the details.
  • Choose a cash sale if you need to close on your own schedule or the house needs repairs, has a tenant issue or is part of an estate.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Homewood houses as they are, and the decision stays with you.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Homewood house if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition and prices in the work. Retail buyers using loans may ask for repairs after an inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Homewood sale?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded at the Jefferson County Probate Court, at either the Birmingham Division or the Bessemer Division. The office cannot prepare the deed for you.

faqs.q: How much is deed tax in Homewood?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value, so a $400,000 sale owes $400 in deed tax, plus a recording fee.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The title company usually prorates the year's bill at closing.
Yes. The census counted 26,414 in 2020 and the Bureau estimates 28,118 for 2025.

faqs.q: Does the Hollywood Historic District change how I sell?
faqs.a: It may affect which buyers are interested, because the district was listed on the National Register in 2002. Ask city hall and a title company about any rules that apply to your address.

faqs.q: What if I am selling a Homewood rental?
faqs.a: You can sell it with or without tenants. Check your lease for notice terms and talk to a title company or attorney about the tenant's rights before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: What documents should I bring to a Homewood closing?
faqs.a: Bring a photo ID, the current deed or trust papers, a lender payoff letter if you have a mortgage, and any keys or garage openers. The title company will tell you if it needs more.
